statement: V8 records which engines actually ran per language (grammar_engine, spellcheck_engine) and degrades to the named fallback. A validator that reports "0 errors" when no engine ran fails this gate.
covers: EC-PACK-14 — V8 run on Japanese: LanguageTool ja has 735 grammar rules and no spell checker, the exact inverse of what deep/10 states. The degradation is spellcheck_engine: none, not grammar_engine: none (ADV 10/R1).
why_these_inputs: Every case below produces the same headline number — zero grammar errors — and they are not the same result. Two of them are a clean course, three of them are a machine that checked nothing, and one is a course whose last validation run crashed halfway. A V8 that returns an empty finding list for all six is the failure this invariant is named for, and it is green in CI.
runlog_note_shape: Each case is the `notes` object of a G6 runlog entry, exactly as coursekit/stages/g6_validate_language.py writes it. `g6_status` is the entry's status. `expect` is what V8 must do with it.

cases.name: no G6 entry at all
cases.because: Nothing ran, and V8 has no basis to report anything. This is the cheapest way to a green pack with an unvalidated course: skip the stage.

cases.name: every engine present, nothing found

notes.backtranslation_engine: agent_rubric/v1 (agent-authored rubric score, not a model round-trip)

cases.because: This is the one case where zero errors is a pass: four engines, 112 candidates, nothing wrong. Without it the gate could be satisfied by failing everything.

cases.name: no engine that can find an error
cases.because: Identical output to the case above and it means the opposite. This is the literal sentence in the invariant.

cases.name: Japanese: grammar rules, no spell checker

notes.backtranslation_engine: agent_rubric/v1 (agent-authored rubric score, not a model round-trip)

cases.expect: no blocking finding, and an info finding naming the missing spell checker
cases.because: R1. LanguageTool Japanese is 735 XML grammar rules and no spell check — the inverse of deep/10 §S6, which had V8 degrading to grammar_engine: none. Probed against a local 6.6 server on 2026-09-12, a nonce token in a Japanese sentence raised no match at all while the same probe in Spanish raised MORFOLOGIK_RULE_ES. A V8 that blocks here would refuse to ship Japanese for a fact that is not true; one that says nothing hides a real, named degradation from the manifest.

cases.name: grammar engine missing, degradation named

notes.backtranslation_engine: agent_rubric/v1 (agent-authored rubric score, not a model round-trip)

cases.expect: no blocking finding, and a warning naming perplexity_only
cases.because: scope2/00 §2.4: V8 'degrades to perplexity-only'. Nobody started the sidecar; perplexity still ran over 112 candidates and rejected three. That is a weaker claim, not a false one — and the manifest has to carry which of the two this pack got.

cases.name: grammar engine missing, degradation NOT named
cases.because: 'and degrades to the named fallback' is the second half of the invariant. An unnamed degradation reaches the manifest as a full-strength V8 pass.

cases.name: an engine field missing from the entry

notes.backtranslation_engine: agent_rubric/v1 (agent-authored rubric score, not a model round-trip)

cases.because: spellcheck_engine is absent, not 'none'. An absent key is an unanswered question; treating it as a default would make every pre-INV-PACK-14 runlog read as fully validated.

cases.name: G6 ran and failed
cases.because: A failed stage checked an unknown fraction of the candidates. Partial coverage reports the same zero as none.

cases.name: every engine present, nothing checked

notes.backtranslation_engine: agent_rubric/v1 (agent-authored rubric score, not a model round-trip)

cases.because: The other half of the same lie. Four engines were up and none of them was handed a sentence; the runlog looks fully equipped and the course is unchecked.
